question:
In the process of bisecting angle BAC in the given figure, why do we draw arcs from points D and E?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c6d9359c85047e2acfaaa113677f0ebb6c04476eda4dc86c4b9cf1c3dfd36c32.png]
solution:
The correct answer is __to intersect above A**(Option 2)**.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Arcs are drawn__ from points D and E to intersect above A.
 
• It ensures precise bisection of the angle BAC by marking the intersection point.
 
• The intersection point serves as a reference for drawing the angle bisector.
 
• By using this method, the bisection is accurate and geometrically valid.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Steps to Bisect an Angle:**

 
 
• Place the compass pointer at the vertex of the angle (point A).
 
• Draw an arc that intersects both arms of the angle at points D and E.
 
• With the compass, draw arcs from points D and E to intersect above A.
 
• Draw a straight line from the vertex (A) through the intersection point of the arcs.
 
 
 
• This line is the angle bisector.
